rus-design-basis-one-ancilla: Abstract, p.1: the paper states its own basis (Clifford+T, one ancilla, measurement). Repeated in the Introduction.
cost-measured-in-t-gates: RUS Circuits, p.1: the paper fixes its own cost metric (T gates) and gives its reason.
t-count-t-depth-definitions: p.2: 'We refer to ... as the T-count ... T-depth' is the paper's own naming of the terms.
scope-axial-rotations: p.2: the paper states that its RUS algorithms are developed for axial rotations, and non-axial V is reduced by Eq (2) (cited from [17]).
open-problem-direct-two-qubit-design: p.2: the paper says direct synthesis for non-axial V is possible in principle, but that practical use is an open problem. The value matches the passage.
cyclotomic-ring-definition: Background, p.2: the paper defines Z[omega], omega = e^{i pi/4}, and its elements a w^3 + b w^2 + c w + d. The value matches.
fig2-comparison-setup: Figure 2 caption, p.2: states the comparison setup (H,T circuits of T-depth at most 8 against RUS protocols of expected T-depth at most 7.5). The value states only the setup, not the counts.
distance-metric-definition: Overview of the Algorithm, p.2: the paper adopts the invariant metric d(V,V') (cited to [20]) as its own measure. The text layer drops the square root and primes, and the value says so. Stated as the paper's chosen metric, not a result.
stage2-algorithm-hyperparameters: Stage 2, p.3 and Figure 3: the paper defines its own algorithm and names delta and sz as its hyperparameters. The value matches Figure 3's input list.
simulation-setup-random-angles: Simulation Results, p.4: 1000 random angles in (0, pi/2) at 25 precisions 1e-11 to 1e-35. The paper states its own experimental setup.
future-work-lower-bounds: Conclusions, p.4: the authors state that the lower bounds do not yet cover the generalized RUS designs. It is a statement of what the work leaves out.
appendix-a-delta-threshold: Appendix A, p.6: the authors state that their analysis only ensures a threshold eps_delta for fixed delta, and that it is likely impractically tight for small delta. Both sentences are caveats on their own method. The guarantee itself is not graded, only that the paper states this limit.
appendix-a-lower-bound-specific: Appendix A, p.6: the paper says the lower bound is specific to its RUS design and that a uniform bound is future work. The value matches.
lemma-1-iff-condition: Lemma 1, Appendix C, p.6: stated with its conditions (theta real, z cyclotomic integer, a,b,c,d integers). The proof is by direct complex expansion of i e^{-i theta/2}(z* - e^{i theta} z), also given on p.3. A short proof that stands in the paper, with no cited step.
observation-2-cyclotomic-size: Observation 2, Appendix C, p.6: stated with its condition 0<|theta|<pi/2 and proved in the paper. The proof applies the classical simultaneous Diophantine approximation theorem (Schmidt, Theorem 1C, [26]) with n=3. That is a textbook tool, not another paper's lemma, so it does not make the item LOW. The coordinator may override if Theorem 1C counts as a specific cited theorem.
appendix-d-random-search-v2: Appendix D.1, p.7 and Figure 7: the paper defines its second normalization algorithm and its inputs. The 'near-deterministic' purpose is stated in the same paragraph.
appendix-d-open-number-theory: Appendix D, p.7: the authors say the solvability chance is an open and likely very hard problem, which they do not attempt to solve, and rely on a conjecture. The value matches the full passage.
definition-5-t-code: Definition 5, Appendix E, p.8: the paper defines a T code.
appendix-f-controlled-pauli-worst-case: Appendix F, p.10: the authors state a worst case of 2t controlled-Pauli gates and that many of them could be a concern on some hardware. A caveat about their own construction.
fourier-angles-setup: Appendix H.1, p.11: 40 angles pi/2^k, k=2 to 41, at 30 precisions 1e-11 to 1e-40. The paper states its own setup.
runtime-implementation-mathematica: Appendix H.2, p.11: Mathematica with a customized PSLQ from [22]. The paper states its own implementation.
runtime-no-wall-clock: Appendix H.2, p.11: the authors state that the code is not optimized for clock speed, so they report PSLQ iterations, not wall clock time. The caveat is about their own measurement.
one-ancilla-not-established: Appendix I.2, p.13: the authors say they could not establish that one ancilla suffices and only sketch a heuristic. The value matches.
dickson-conjecture-unproven: Appendix I.2, p.14: the paper states that its one-ancilla argument reduces to Dickson's conjecture, which is unproven. This is the limit of its own argument.
sxy-definition: Appendix I.3, p.14: the paper defines Sxy by its formula and states the geometric reading (rotations about axes in the xy-plane). The value matches.
lemma-22-bell-eigenstates: Lemma 22, Appendix I.3, p.14: both conditions are quoted. The singlet part cites the textbook fact in [17, Section 2.6] (Nielsen and Chuang), a standard tool. The Sxy part is proved by explicit computation, and I rechecked it by hand: V^dagger tensor V maps Psi+ to Psi+.

theory_low.rus-expected-cost-formula: textbook, stated not proved (F129): Eq (1), p.1, is introduced with 'It is easy to see'. No derivation is given.
theory_low.stage2-sample-size-inference: Stage 2, p.3: the sample size O(delta L1^2) is inferred from a conjecture the paper says it has only 'supporting empirical evidence' for. A conditional inference, not a proved result.
theory_low.stage2-expected-cost-bound: Stage 2, p.3: the bound holds 'for such r', and those r are assumed to exist by the unproven conjecture. No proof is given.
theory_low.stage4-t-count-up-to-9: Stage 4, p.4: a summary of Theorem 4 (Appendix E, p.7 to p.9). Theorem 4's proof uses [19] for the T-count of controlled gates and Lemma 9, which rests on [14]. See theorem-4-two-qubit-t-count.
theory_low.generalized-designs-claim: Simulation Results, p.4: a summary claim that points to Appendix I. The authors' claim about 'tight control over the T-depth' is graded at the Appendix I items, and the proof there is graded LOW.
theory_low.appendix-a-necessary-condition: Appendix A, p.5 to p.6: an informal counting argument with O() estimates, made under a 'temporarily' assumed solvable norm equation. The constant K is not derived. Not a stated and proved result.
theory_low.appendix-d-example-3: Example 3, Appendix D, p.7: a worked example with a garbled factorization line. The criterion for 'good' primes (p.7) makes 3 and 5 look like bad primes with odd powers in the factorization as printed, yet the paper names only 7. Text layer exponents are unreliable, so the claim is not settled by the passage.
theory_low.theorem-4-two-qubit-t-count: Theorem 4, Appendix E, p.7 to p.9: the proof uses [19] (Giles and Selinger) for the T-count 2 of Lambda(w^-1 S) and Lambda(H) ('by known methods (c.f. [19])'). It also rests on Lemma 9, whose proof uses the canonical-form algorithm of [14]. A cited specific result is a step, so it is not a proved result under the rule.
theory_low.lemma-9-normal-form: Lemma 9, Appendix E, p.8: the proof starts from [14], which defines canonical T,H circuits and gives the algorithm that rewrites any circuit to that form. It then adds an induction on syllables. A specific cited algorithm of [14] is a step, so LOW.
theory_low.lemma-10-identities: textbook, stated not proved (F129): Lemma 10, p.8, lists gate identities 'established by direct computation'. No computation is shown.
theory_low.lemma-11-decoration: Lemma 11, Appendix E, p.8 to p.9: the induction on t is in the paper, but its first step applies Lemma 9, whose proof rests on the canonical-form algorithm of [14]. The paper does not settle it alone.
theory_low.corollary-12-t-code-relation: Corollary 12, Appendix E, p.9: no proof is written. It follows from Lemmas 9 and 11, which rest on [14] through Lemma 9.
theory_low.lemma-14-jack-of-daggers: Lemma 14, Appendix E, p.9: the proof calls the procedure of Lemma 11 (which rests on Lemma 9 and [14]) and says 'It is easy to see' for the circuit. Not settled by the paper alone.
theory_low.corollary-15-rus-rotation: Corollary 15, Appendix E, p.9 to p.10: the proof gets the T-count t+9 from Theorem 4, whose proof uses [19] and Lemma 9 (which rests on [14]). The success probability |u|^2 is a direct computation that the paper only asserts.
theory_low.observation-17-pauli-count: Observation 17, Appendix E, p.10: the argument is a pigeonhole sketch that gives no explicit rewriting, and the printed commutation rule for Y H is wrong in the text layer. A sketch, not a proof.
theory_low.total-runtime-polylog-claim: Appendix H.2, p.12: an argument that cites [24, 27, 29, 30] for the norm equation cost, says 'It is easy to see' for the search count, and depends on the unproven conjecture of Stage 2. No wall clock runtime is reported.
theory_low.appendix-i-three-ancilla-design-summary: Appendix I, p.12: an overview claim. The factor 3 in T-count is not derived in I.3, whose Theorem 23 bounds T-depth, not T-count. The 'two additional ancillas' versus the section title '3 ancillas' (two plus the RUS one) is left to the reader.
theory_low.theorem-18-two-ancillas: Theorem 18, Appendix I.1, p.12 to p.13: the proof uses [19, Theorem 1] (exact Clifford+T implementation with one ancilla) and [19, Lemma 7] (avoiding that ancilla). It also uses Lemma 19 cited from [31, Theorem 6.9]. Specific cited results are steps, so LOW. The statement and conditions are quoted correctly.
theory_low.corollary-20-two-ancillas-no-correction: Corollary 20, Appendix I.1, p.13: the proof is a one-line appeal to Theorem 18, and the claim that a RUS circuit gives alpha with alpha V in Z[i,1/sqrt2] is asserted, not shown. Theorem 18 is LOW because it uses [19].
theory_low.corollary-21-cyclotomic-field-unitaries: Corollary 21, Appendix I.1, p.13: the proof clears denominators by a Galois norm argument, then applies Theorem 18, which uses [19, Theorem 1 and Lemma 7]. It rests on a cited step.
theory_low.theorem-23-t-depth-bound: Theorem 23, Appendix I.3, p.14 to p.15: the proof is 'an inspection' of Figure 11 and uses the controlled-SWAP of [36] (7 T gates, T-depth 4) as a step. The T-depth bound t+8 therefore rests on a cited construction.
